title: Nonrelativistic Spin-Orbit-Coupling Effects in Odd-Parity Coplanar Magnets
authors: Dongling Liu, Zheng-Yang Zhuang, Di Zhu, Zhigang Wu, Zhongbo Yan
abstract: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) is a relativistic effect that underpins a broad spectrum of phenomena in condensed matter physics, from topological phases of matter to spintronic functionality. Its relativistic origin, however, restricts strong SOC to heavy-element materials and locks spin-momentum texture into a fixed, material-specific pattern. Here we show that odd-parity coplanar magnets offer a nonrelativistic pathway to highly tunable SOC effects. We construct a bilayer coplanar magnet via symmetry-guided stacking of two monolayer odd-parity altermagnets and demonstrate that Rashba, Weyl, and Dresselhaus spin textures can all be realized, and that the spin texture can be switched between these forms simply by tuning the layer Neel vector. Through the spin Edelstein effect and the realization of fully gapped chiral topological superconducting phases, we demonstrate that this nonrelativistic SOC achieves physical equivalence to its relativistic counterpart. Our findings identify a new class of odd-parity coplanar magnets as a versatile platform for engineering SOC effects.
summary: The authors propose that odd-parity coplanar magnets offer a nonrelativistic route to engineering strong Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC) effects. By constructing a bilayer system and tuning its magnetic order, they demonstrate the realization of distinct Rashba, Weyl, and Dresselhaus spin textures. This work is significant because it shows this engineered SOC can achieve physical equivalence to its relativistic counterparts while offering unprecedented tunability.
main_problem: To find a nonrelativistic pathway to highly tunable Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC) effects, overcoming the limitation that strong SOC is typically restricted to heavy elements and fixed by material symmetry.
main_result: The proposed odd-parity coplanar magnet bilayer realizes Rashba, Weyl, and Dresselhaus spin textures nonrelativistically, achieving physical equivalence to relativistic SOC via superconducting phases.
method: Symmetry analysis combined with k.p expansion and projection onto low-energy continuum Hamiltonians was used to derive effective models for the system's electronic structure.
model_or_system: The model is an odd-parity coplanar magnet realized as a bilayer stack of two monolayer antiferromagnets, described by a multi-band Hamiltonian incorporating interlayer coupling and magnetic order parameters.
key_observables: Rashba, Weyl, and Dresselhaus spin textures ($\langle s_x(\mathbf{k}) angle, \langle s_y(\mathbf{k}) angle$), Spin Edelstein Effect susceptibility ($\chi_{ij}$), and the existence of fully gapped chiral topological superconducting phases.
important_parameters: Layer Néel vector tuning (used to switch SOC types); magnetic field ($B$) relative to pairing gap ($\Delta$); interlayer coupling ($\eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on symmetry requirements for the nonrelativistic mechanism and approximations like linear response theory for transport calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the bilayer stacking strategy, energy spectra showing distinct SOC types (Rashba/Weyl/Dresselhaus), spin textures in momentum space, and topological phase diagrams mapping out superconducting regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the physical model via symmetry-guided stacking, deriving low-energy Hamiltonians for different SOC types, calculating characteristic spin textures and transport responses (SEE), and finally demonstrating the realization of topological superconductivity.
why_interesting: This work provides a mechanism to engineer complex electronic couplings like SOC using structural/magnetic degrees of freedom rather than relying solely on heavy elements or intrinsic material properties, which is highly relevant for designing novel quantum materials.
